helpful: The provisioned petition, BIO and QP text — enough to weigh the split and vehicle arguments without retrieval.
context.json's frozen band/CVSG/distribution state plus the statpack's sal-v4 band table made the anchor a table lookup.
Forward-mode web retrieval of the Solicitor General's brief, which was the single most decisive input.
gaps: The document pipeline does not provision the United States' CVSG brief (or the petitioners' supplemental brief) even though both are on the docket before the snapshot; on a CVSG'd petition the government's recommendation is the dominant signal and had to be fetched and PDF-extracted by hand.
The statpack's CVSG cut does not split by the SG's recommendation (grant vs deny), so the conditional rate this cell needed came from general knowledge rather than the pack.
WebFetch could not read supremecourt.gov PDFs; a text-extraction fallback in the fetcher would remove a manual step.
fedcourts query has no filter for CVSG'd petitions or for a subject like ERISA on SCOTUS rows, so it could not surface comparable priors.
notes: The moment here is unusual: the cell fired after the SG brief and on the day of the third distribution, so the record is far richer than a first-distribution cell's.
